nodes.text: Let $k\geq 2$ and $n_k(p)$ denote the least $k$th power nonresidue of $p$. Is it true that\[\sum_{p<x} n_k(p)\sim c_k \frac{x}{\log x}\]for some constant $c_k>0$?

#980 : [Er65b] number theory Erdős [Er61e] proved this when $k=2$, with\[c_2=\sum_{k=1}^\infty \frac{p_k}{2^k}.\]The general case was proved by Elliott [El67b] .
